newsitem.title: CHINA: China propaganda tsar tightens grip on media.
newsitem.headline: China propaganda tsar tightens grip on media.

text.p: China's powerful propaganda tsar Ding Guan'gen has moved to further tighten the Communist Party's grip on state media in the run-up to a crucial five-yearly party congress.

Ding, head of the party's Propaganda Department, ordered state media to sing the praises of the party to create a favourable atmosphere for the forthcoming 15th party congress, the People's Daily Overseas Edition said on Thursday.
He also called on state media to back Communist Party chief and state president Jiang Zemin, who is eager to assert his authority at the congress.
Propaganda appearing in state media in the run-up to the congress should focus on economic construction and strengthening "spiritual civilisation", Ding said.
Jiang has promoted "spiritual civilisation" as a way to revive communist doctrines of civic responsibility and self-sacrifice eroded by nearly two decades of capitalist-style economic reforms.

Ding made the appeal amid revelations of factional strife among the Communist Party elite that analysts say mark the start of a campaign to discredit leftists opposed to economic reform and Jiang's rule.
China is expected to hold its 15th party congress in late September or early October.
